channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Meta Quest Store Submission Guide for Developers
item.description: A practical guide for VR developers on getting through the Meta Horizon Store review, covering the performance, pause behaviour and data-declaration checks behind most rejections.

item.title: Release candidate: Godot 4.8 RC 1
item.description: Godot 4.8 has entered the release candidate stage with all features locked in and known critical regressions fixed; the team invites production projects to try it after backing up, and asks the community to help test for any remaining major issues.

item.title: Why AI Agents Silently Break Unreal Engine 5.9 Meshes: Projective-Radiometric Null-Space Drift (and How to Catch It Before Save)
item.description: AI agents can declare a mesh edit clean in the viewport and only reveal broken geometry, materials, or hair after saving — this piece breaks down why that silent damage happens and how to catch it before you hit save.

item.title: Generate a Maze With a Guaranteed Solution in Python (API Tutorial)
item.description: A maze generator written carelessly can easily produce an unsolvable level; this tutorial shows how to guarantee a valid path and expose the generator as an API for games.

item.title: Zombies Aren't Real Wiki - Complete Beginner Guide & Defense Strategies
item.description: A beginner's guide roundup for Zombies Aren't Real, a horde-defense tactical game, covering civilian evacuation and defense layouts.

item.title: One rules engine, two languages
item.description: Shows how CheX implements the chess rules engine twice — TypeScript in the browser and Rust on the server — and keeps both in exact agreement on every move, capture, and checkmate.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4 launch boosts Call of Duty HQ to top of Newzoo's PC revenue charts
item.description: The Modern Warfare 4 launch pushed Call of Duty HQ to the top of Newzoo's PC revenue chart, in a month with almost no other major releases.

item.title: Cheese Roll Game - Building a Fast 3D Browser Arcade Downhill Runner
item.description: The author shares how they built a fast, high-performance 3D browser arcade downhill runner with Three.js, covering optimization and game feel.

item.title: The MARROW Project
item.description: A developer is building a game engine called MARROW from scratch to learn how engines work under the hood, with plans to use it for an open-world game later.

item.title: Retention Without a Store: Daily Rewards, Lucky Spin and Boosters Done Kindly
item.description: Using a store-free casual game as an example, this piece shows how daily rewards, lucky spins and boosters can retain players without any purchases — a reference for gentle retention design.

item.title: Turn Raw AI Video Clips into Foot-Anchored Transparent 2D Game Sprites (Godot 4 & Phaser 3)
item.description: While shipping a martial-arts roguelike, the author worked out a pipeline for turning raw AI video clips into foot-anchored, transparent 2D game sprites for Godot 4 and Phaser 3.

item.title: SEO for browser games: 9 fixes to get HTML5 games indexed
item.description: HTML5 game pages are mostly a canvas and a loading bar, so search engines find little to index — here are nine fixes to get browser games discovered.

item.title: Designing Environments That Tell a Story for 007 First Light
item.description: Environment artist Thomas Pulluelo shares how he built atmospheric spaces for the new James Bond game that subtly guide players through gameplay.

item.title: First Week for an Outstaffed Game Developer in India: A Repo, Build and Review Checklist
item.description: When a studio brings an outstaffed developer into its own team, the first week's repo access, build setup and review process decide whether the arrangement works — this checklist covers the engineering side.

item.title: This Blender Tool Lets You Sculpt Directly Along Curves On 3D Surfaces
item.description: A new Blender tool lets you sculpt directly along curves on 3D surfaces, with editable, reusable curves so brushes, strengths and effects can be swapped without starting over.

item.title: Revealed: How much direct-to-consumer revenue games publishers really made in Q3 2026
item.description: Drawing on the latest financials, this analysis revisits how games publishers performed on direct-to-consumer revenue in Q3 2026 — who is still growing off-store sales and who has plateaued.

item.title: Beautiful Shimmering Veil In Blender Inspired By Foundation Title Sequence
item.description: Follow Marinko Tambur's tutorial to recreate the shimmering veil effect from the Foundation title sequence in Blender.

item.title: Excalibur 1.0: pause the game, keep the interface running
item.description: A walkthrough of Excalibur 1.0's pause system and migration tools, covering how to keep menus responsive while the game is paused and how to upgrade an existing TypeScript project.

item.title: Game Audio Format & Magic-Byte Compatibility Matrix (2026): FSB5, WEM, BNK, BFSTM, HCA & XWB
item.description: A 2026 reference table for identifying game audio containers from FMOD, Wwise, Nintendo and CRIWARE by their magic bytes, so you can pick the right decoder before trial and error.

item.title: Why our pool balls sped up mid-roll (and 3 other bugs from a browser pool game)
item.description: A postmortem of four unrelated bugs behind 'the physics feels wrong' in a hand-rolled three.js browser pool game: frame-rate-stepped physics, balls slipping through pocket mouths, AI freezing the game and shaders compiling mid-shot.
